channel.title: Stories – Praveen Kumar Singh Photography
channel.description: The stories behind the photographs: where they were made, what the light was doing, and how they became prints.

item.title: Between water and sky: fifteen seconds on the Seine
item.description:
The moment

At the end of August, Paris comes back to itself. The holidays are ending, the evenings are still warm, and the river is quieter than in high summer.

On 29 August, the sun had set a little before nine. The weather was clear, with beautiful patches of cloud drifting slowly across the sky. By half past, the last blue was leaving it, the Eiffel Tower was lit gold, and across the water the windows of the tall towers on the Left Bank were switching on, one by one.

I was standing on the Pont Mirabeau. I chose it for its panoramic view: from the middle of the bridge the Seine opens up towards the tower, with the river, the islands, the bridges and the city all in one wide frame.

Below the tower, at the tip of the Île aux Cygnes, stands the small Statue of Liberty that the American community in Paris gave to the city in 1889. From where I stood it is only a green silhouette against the bridge, easy to miss until you know it is there.

Making the photograph

At night the river never stands still: boats pass, the current moves, the wind ripples the surface. To turn all that movement into calm, I kept the shutter open for fifteen seconds.

During those fifteen seconds the ripples blur into a smooth surface, and the lights become long, soft reflections: gold under the tower, blue and amber under the boats and the buildings. The clouds move too, so the sky becomes gentler than it looked to the eye.

I used my Nikon Z5II with the NIKKOR Z 24–200 mm lens at 48 mm, at f/10 and ISO 100. A low ISO keeps the shadows clean, and f/10 keeps everything sharp, from the water in front to the top of the tower. An exposure this long needs the camera to be completely still, so it stood on my tripod in the middle of the bridge.

The print

The title, Reflections of Desire: Parisian Nights Between Water and Sky, comes from that meeting of the two: the city’s lights above, and their slower, softer echo in the river.

This photograph is available as a limited edition of only 5 prints, each signed and numbered, with a certificate of authenticity. You can find the limited edition on Saatchi Art and Artfinder, or enquire about buying it directly.

Open-edition prints are also available on Saatchi Art and Photo4me.
